facts.title: A 747 Lost All Four Engines After Flying Into a Volcanic Ash Cloud
facts.summary: On December 15, 1989, KLM Flight 867 flew into an ash cloud from Alaska's Redoubt Volcano, and all four engines of the 747 jetliner flamed out.

facts.title: A Mexican Farmer Watched a New Volcano Burst Out of His Cornfield
facts.summary: On February 20, 1943, farmer Dionisio Pulido and his wife Paula were burning brush in their cornfield in Michoacán, Mexico, when the ground in front of them swelled, cracked open and began to hiss.

facts.summary: On November 13, 1985, Colombia's Nevado del Ruiz had a relatively small eruption, yet it caused the second-deadliest volcanic disaster of the 20th century.

facts.title: About Three-Quarters of Earth's Volcanic Activity Happens Deep Underwater
facts.summary: Most of Earth's volcanic activity happens where nobody can see it.

facts.title: Hawaiian Lava Can Stretch Into Golden Strands of Glass Called Pele's Hair
facts.summary: Pele's hair is not hair at all but strands of volcanic glass.

facts.title: Jupiter's Moon Io Is the Most Volcanically Active World in the Solar System
facts.summary: Jupiter's moon Io is the most volcanically active world in the solar system, with hundreds of volcanoes.

facts.title: Mauna Loa Rises About 30,000 Feet From the Seafloor, Higher Than Everest
facts.summary: Mauna Loa on Hawaiʻi Island is the largest active volcano on the planet.

facts.summary: When Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines exploded on June 15, 1991, it changed the temperature of the entire Earth.

facts.title: Tambora's 1815 Eruption Led to the "Year Without a Summer"
facts.summary: The cold "year without a summer" of 1816 began on the other side of the world.

facts.title: The 20th Century's Largest Eruption Came From a Brand-New Alaskan Volcano
facts.summary: The largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century burst from a new volcano, Novarupta, in Alaska on June 6, 1912.

facts.title: Tonga's 2022 Eruption Punched a Plume Into the Mesosphere
facts.summary: On January 15, 2022, the undersea volcano Hunga Tonga-Hunga Haʻapai sent a plume of gas, steam and ash 58 kilometers (36 miles) into the sky.

facts.title: Yellowstone's Biggest Eruption Left a Caldera More Than 60 Miles Across
facts.summary: About 2.1 million years ago, Yellowstone produced one of the five largest individual volcanic eruptions known anywhere on Earth.
